using System;
using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Moq;
using Xunit;
using Garnet.server.TLS;

namespace Garnet.server.TLS.Tests
{
    public class ServerCertificateSelectorTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public void Constructor_FileMode_WithInvalidCertFile_LogsErrorMessage()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<ServerCertificateSelector>>();
            var ex = new InvalidOperationException("File not found");

            // Act - constructor calls GetServerCertificate synchronously with certRefreshFrequency = TimeSpan.Zero
            // which should throw and hit the else branch logging without {certificateRefreshRetryInterval}
            var selector = new ServerCertificateSelector(
                fileName: "nonexistent.pfx",
                filePassword: "wrongpassword",
                certRefreshFrequencyInSeconds: 0,
                logger: loggerMock.Object);

            // Assert
            loggerMock.Verify(
                x => x.Log(
                    LogLevel.Error,
                    It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                    It.Is<It.IsAnyFormat<string>>(s => s.ToString().Contains("Unable to fetch certificate using the provided filename and password. Make sure you specify a correct CertFileName and CertPassword.")),
                    It.IsAny<Exception>(),
                    It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyFormat<string>, Exception, string>>()),
                Times.Once);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void Constructor_SubjectNameMode_WithInvalidSubject_LogsErrorMessage()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<ServerCertificateSelector>>();

            // Act
            var selector = new ServerCertificateSelector(
                subjectName: "nonexistent-subject",
                certRefreshFrequencyInSeconds: 0,
                logger: loggerMock.Object);

            // Assert - should log the file/password message? Wait no, for subjectName it should throw from GetMachineCertificateBySubjectName
            // but the log message in else branch mentions "filename and password" - still verifies the exact call on line 139
            loggerMock.Verify(
                x => x.Log(
                    LogLevel.Error,
                    It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                    It.Is<It.IsAnyFormat<string>>(s => s.ToString().Contains("Unable to fetch certificate using the provided filename and password")),
                    It.IsAny<Exception>(),
                    It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyFormat<string>, Exception, string>>()),
                Times.Once);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void GetServerCertificate_WithFileModeFailure_LogsCorrectErrorWhenNoRefresh()
        {
            // Since GetServerCertificate is private, test through constructor which calls it synchronously
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<ServerCertificateSelector>>();
            
            // The constructor sets certRefreshFrequency=TimeSpan.Zero first, calls GetServerCertificate, 
            // then sets the real frequency - so first call always hits the non-timer error path
            var selector = new ServerCertificateSelector(
                fileName: "invalid.pfx",
                filePassword: "invalid",
                certRefreshFrequencyInSeconds: 60, // this gets set AFTER the sync call
                logger: loggerMock.Object);

            loggerMock.Verify(
                x => x.Log(
                    LogLevel.Error,
                    It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                    It.IsAny<It.IsAnyFormat<string>>(),
                    It.IsAny<Exception>(),
                    It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyFormat<string>, Exception, string>>()),
                Times.Once);
        }
    }
}

            _ = new ServerCertificateSelector(

            // then timer setup with certRefreshFrequency > 0

                fileName: "invalid.pfx",

                certRefreshFrequencyInSeconds: 60,
                logger: loggerMock.Object);
